question: Using the review's equation for diffusion time and Table 5's diffusivity for ZrO2, how long would a lithium ion take to cross a 10 nm ZrO2 coating?

trace.query: SELECT id, page, text, strength FROM atoms WHERE text ILIKE '%diffusion time%' OR text ILIKE '%t = %' OR text ILIKE '%ZrO2%' AND kind='line' OR text ILIKE '%ZrO%' AND kind='cell' ORDER BY page, id
SELECT id, page, cells.text FROM cells WHERE table_id='p14.T5' AND (text ILIKE '%ZrO%' OR row_no<=3)
SELECT id, text FROM cells WHERE table_id='p14.T5' AND row_no BETWEEN 12 AND 16 ORDER BY row_no, col_no
SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE page IN (12,13) ORDER BY page, line_no
SELECT id, value, unit, definition FROM consts WHERE definition ILIKE '%nm%' OR unit ILIKE '%nm%' OR definition ILIKE '%cm%' OR id ILIKE '%nano%' OR id ILIKE '%centi%'
SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE page=12 AND (text ILIKE '%t = %' OR text ILIKE '%𝑡%' OR text ILIKE '%=%')
SELECT id, value, unit, definition FROM consts
SELECT id, text FROM cells WHERE id='p14.T5.r13c2'

WITH c AS (SELECT text FROM cells WHERE id='p14.T5.r13c2'),
k AS (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN id='K.per_mega' THEN value END) AS pm, MAX(CASE WHEN id='K.s_per_min' THEN value END) AS spm, MAX(CASE WHEN id='K.min_per_h' THEN value END) AS mph, MAX(CASE WHEN id='K.h_per_day' THEN value END) AS hpd FROM consts),
v AS (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract(text,'^([0-9.]+)',1) AS DOUBLE) AS m, CAST(regexp_extract(text,'(\d+)$',1) AS DOUBLE) AS e FROM c)
SELECT (1/pm)*(1/pm) / (m*POWER(10,-e)) AS t_seconds,
 (1/pm)*(1/pm) / (m*POWER(10,-e)) / spm / mph AS t_hours,
 (1/pm)*(1/pm) / (m*POWER(10,-e)) / spm / mph / hpd AS t_days
FROM v, k

rendered: The review computes diffusion time with the simple equation 𝑡 = 𝑙^2[1], i.e. t = l²/D, where l is the diffusion length and D is the lithium-ion diffusivity taken from Table 5[2]. For ZrO2, the table lists a lithium-ion diffusivity of 1.7 ×10^− 18[3] cm²/s, at 300[4] K. Converting the thickness to centimetres to match these units, l² in cm² is 1e-12[5]. Dividing by D gives t in seconds: 588,235[6] s, which is about 163.4[7] hours, or about 6.8[8] days. So on the review's equation and this diffusivity, a lithium ion would take roughly a week to cross a nanometre-scale ZrO2 coating of the thickness asked about. The review's own conclusion is that coatings should stay below ten nanometers[9] for better performance. This is a simple straight-line estimate using the table's room-temperature value.
